title: Does division in the nematic fuel-cell rods follow the exterior fuel diffusion length, whether the slow exterior comes from the ring or from the medium?
summary: c15 found that a ringless twin with fuel slowed only outside the rods matches the self-made ring's division gain, and that edge fuel, not core fuel, tracks division. Diffusion-limited (Mullins-Sekerka) division (Zwicker et al. 2017) predicts that the split rate depends on the exterior supply length l = sqrt(Dout/kdf) and on nothing else. A collapse of the ring and twin data onto one curve would be a K law and would settle what a wall must do to beat the twin.
experiment: In 20261025T1713-c15-fuelcell-outslow-twin's world, sweep the exterior fuel diffusivity (4 values over 30x) in the ringless twin, and the ring adsorption strength beta (3 values) in the ringed world, on seeds 0-1 at t=1000. Measure the effective exterior D at each rod edge from the fuel profile, and the persistent splits per rod-time. Plot splits against l. Law if both arms fall on one curve within seed scatter.
